paragraphs: Brandkit gives an organization one searchable, shareable home for its logos, guidelines, images, video, presentations, stories and press releases. It bundles a brand portal, media center, brand guidelines, digital asset management, a CMS, a knowledge library and file transfer into one system. The buyers it names include national and local government agencies, tourism boards, place brands, economic development agencies, universities and franchises.

Uploaded assets are organized with automatic tagging and metadata generated by AI. Search combines multi-faceted keywords with AI-powered semantic search. Brand guidelines, rights management and licensing information surface alongside the assets themselves. The platform also generates llms.txt and llms.html plain text files so chatbots and language models can read the content. Pricing is based on usage rather than per seat, which the company ties to public sector bodies sharing resources with many end users.

The founder writes that Brandkit began in 1994 to fix the same problem it addresses now. The company says it is still privately held, has never taken outside money, and is profitable. It says it runs brand hubs, media centres, image libraries and partner toolkits for tourism boards, place brands, universities and government departments. One published case study covers how VisitScotland built a media library across several organisations.

quote.text: We started Brandkit in 1994 to fix exactly this.
